chunks: Isma'il ibn Mansur ibn Ahmad al-Qassar in Furqani narrated to us, saying: Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ja'far ibn al-Hasan ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them both) narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari, Abu Ali, narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhal narred to us, from Thalabah ibn Maymun, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hajjaj, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the words of God, the Exalted: '...Take your adornment at every masjid...' He said: Combing attracts sustenance, improves the hair, fulfills needs, increases semen, and cuts phlegm. The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) would comb under his chin forty times, and above it seven times, and say: 'It increases intellect and cuts phlegm.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of combing according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes the verse 'Take your adornment at every masjid' (7:31) by interpreting 'adornment' not merely as ritual purity but as physical grooming, specifically combing, which serves as a means of attracting sustenance (rizq) and fulfilling needs. This narration highlights the Prophetic tradition of combing the beard to enhance intellect (dhikn) and health, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of physical well-being with spiritual discipline.
